title: The Unannounced Inspection
text: A health inspector walks in at the worst hour of service and asks to see the walk-in.

choices.label: Stop service, walk them through everything

outcome.narration: You kill the tickets and open every door. It costs you a night and buys you a clean file.
You run two jobs at once and get away with it.
The inspector notices you are managing them instead of answering them.
You pay for the gasket, the thermometer and the log book. Boring, and it never bites you again.

title: Table for One, Under Another Name
text: A critic has booked under a name that is not theirs. You recognise the face at the door.

choices.label: Cook your actual menu, say nothing

outcome.narration: They write it up as it was. As it was turns out to be good.
An average night, recorded permanently.

choices.label: Send out the best of everything

outcome.narration: You cook for one table and everyone else eats second. The review is warm and the kitchen knows why.

title: The Algorithm Moved
text: The marketplace reshuffles its rankings overnight. You were page one. You are now page four.

choices.label: Buy your way back with ads

outcome.narration: You rent the position you used to own.
It hurts for two quarters. After that the margin is yours and so is the customer list.
You wait. The ranking does not come back on its own.

title: The Return That Comes Back Empty
text: Dozens of returns, all the same excuse, all from addresses two streets apart. The boxes come back with the wrong thing inside.

outcome.narration: The fraud stops. So do some honest returns, and those customers tell people.
A tool catches the pattern you were catching by hand. Honest customers never notice it exists.

choices.label: Eat it, keep the policy generous

outcome.narration: You decide the cost of being easy to deal with is a line item you can carry. For now.

title: The Email From The Researcher
text: A stranger emails a working exploit against your login, a 90-day disclosure deadline, and a polite tone.

choices.label: Fix it, credit them, publish the writeup

outcome.narration: You fix it in nine days and say so out loud. Engineers who read that email start applying to work for you.
The hole closes. Nobody outside the room learns it was open.
You threaten the person who was helping you. The exploit is still there, and now the deadline is public.

title: The Job That Ran All Weekend
text: Somebody left a job running on Friday. The cloud invoice arrives Monday.

choices.label: Pay it, add hard spend caps

outcome.narration: You pay, then you cap it so the same weekend cannot happen twice.

choices.label: Beg the provider for a credit

outcome.narration: Two calls and an apology later, most of it is written off.
They are sympathetic and they invoice you anyway.
You find them. Everyone watches you find them, and learns not to tell you things.

title: The Back Catalogue Goes Dark
text: The platform demonetises three years of uploads over a policy you cannot get a human to explain.

choices.label: Appeal, and post about the appeal

outcome.narration: The appeal goes nowhere for six weeks. The video about the appeal does numbers.

choices.label: Move the audience to something you own

outcome.narration: A fraction of them follow you. That fraction cannot be demonetised by anybody.

choices.label: Re-cut everything to fit the policy

outcome.narration: Three years of work, sanded down until it complies. It is duller and it earns.

title: The Sponsor With Notes
text: A brand offers more than a year of revenue. They want approval over what you say about the category.

outcome.narration: The money lands. The next time you praise something, the audience checks who paid.
They fold on the notes and keep the budget. It happens more often than people think.
They walk. You keep the thing that made them want you.
You post the offer with the numbers blacked out. The audience decides you are theirs.

title: Worn Without Asking
text: Someone famous wears your piece to something enormous. You did not send it and they did not credit you.

outcome.narration: You name the piece, price it up and put every unit you can finance behind the moment.

choices.label: Stay quiet and let it build

outcome.narration: You say nothing. The people who find it themselves feel like they found something.

choices.label: Reach out and ask for a real partnership

outcome.narration: They say yes. A year of marketing arrives in one afternoon.
Their team never replies. The photograph still exists.

title: Your Piece, Someone Else's Label
text: A marketplace is full of your best piece at a third of the price, stitched badly, sold under six different names.

outcome.narration: You take down forty listings. Sixty go up. You keep doing it because stopping is worse.

choices.label: Compete on what a fake cannot copy

outcome.narration: Better fabric, real labels, a repair promise. The counterfeits stay cheap and start looking cheap.

choices.label: Ignore it — it is free advertising

outcome.narration: Thousands of people meet your design through a bad copy of it, and judge you on the seams.

title: The Community Reads The Patch Notes
text: You changed how the shop works. The forum has organised, the reviews are moving, and they are not wrong.

choices.label: Revert it and post the reasoning

outcome.narration: You roll it back and explain what you were trying to fix. They believe you, this time.
The numbers go up and the loudest thousand players leave. Both of those are permanent.

choices.label: Split the difference in a dev stream

outcome.narration: Two hours live, answering the hard version of every question. Nobody is thrilled. Everybody stays.

title: Someone Broke It In Four Minutes
text: A speedrunner finishes your game in four minutes using a wall you forgot to close. The clip has a million views.

outcome.narration: The wall closes. The community mourns the wall.

choices.label: Leave it in and make it official

outcome.narration: You add a leaderboard for it. The bug becomes a mode, and the mode sells copies.

choices.label: Hire the runner to break the rest of it

outcome.narration: They find eleven more in a fortnight. It is the best QA money you have ever spent.

title: The Rack Gave Way
text: A member is hurt on your equipment. Not badly. It was your rack and your fault.

choices.label: Own it, pay the bills, replace everything

outcome.narration: You call them yourself, cover what insurance will not, and re-kit the floor. It is expensive and it is the answer.
The claim is processed correctly by people who have never met them.
You are legally fine. Your coaches heard how you talked about a member who got hurt.

title: January
text: Sign-ups triple in three weeks. The floor is full at six, the showers have a queue, and your regulars are quietly furious.

choices.label: Cap membership and start a waitlist

outcome.narration: You stop selling. Scarcity does the marketing and your regulars get their gym back.
A very good quarter. By April the new ones have stopped coming and some of the old ones have too.
You buy capacity with hours nobody wants to work. The schedule holds. The coaches are tired.

title: The Dermatologist With A Camera
text: A dermatologist with a large following reads your ingredient list out loud, line by line, on video.

choices.label: Send them the full formulation and the data

outcome.narration: They post a correction and a recommendation. An expert defending you is worth more than any campaign.
They read the data and stand by the video. They had a point about the fragrance.
Six weeks and a new base. The product is better and the old stock is a write-off.
The video is now the top result for your product name.

title: Prove The Claim
text: A regulator asks you to substantiate the word on the front of the bottle. You have a study. It is small.

outcome.narration: It costs a quarter of your cash and it means the word on the bottle is true. Nobody can take it off you now.
"Helps improve" replaces "reduces". The bottle is legal and it sells less.

choices.label: Submit the small study and hope

outcome.narration: It is accepted. You get to keep the word and the quiet knowledge of how thin the evidence was.
Rejected, with a fine and a public notice. The notice is the expensive part.

title: The District Pilot
text: A district will pilot you across forty schools. Procurement wants a year of data retention promises and a price that assumes you win.

outcome.narration: Forty schools and a logo you can put on every deck. The margin is thin enough to see through.

choices.label: Hold your price, offer a smaller pilot

outcome.narration: Six schools instead of forty, at a price that works. They come back next year for the rest.
You get your quarter back. Somebody else becomes the district's default.

title: They Are Using It To Cheat
text: Your fastest-growing use case turns out to be students getting answers without learning anything. Engagement has never looked better.

choices.label: Rebuild it to show working, not answers

outcome.narration: Usage halves. The students who stay actually learn, and teachers start recommending you by name.

choices.label: Leave it and stop looking at that number

outcome.narration: Growth is excellent. You are running an education company that is measurably bad at education.
You do not stop the cheating. You make it visible to the one person who can.

title: The Audit Arrives
text: Your certifier wants the full chain of custody for every input. You have paperwork for most of it.

outcome.narration: Eleven suppliers, four countries, six weeks. You pass, and the certificate finally means what customers think it means.
Conditional pass, with a note to do better next cycle.
Certification suspended pending review. The badge comes off the packaging and the packaging is the pitch.

choices.label: Drop the certification, tell the truth instead

outcome.narration: You publish what you actually know and what you do not. It costs shelf space and buys something harder to fake.

title: Margin Or Mission
text: Your biggest investor has run the numbers. Drop the recycled input and the gross margin fixes itself.

outcome.narration: You put it in a board memo so it cannot be relitigated quietly. The investor is cold for a year.

choices.label: Switch the input, keep the marketing

outcome.narration: The margin arrives immediately. The claim on the box is now a thing you hope nobody checks.
You explain the tradeoff publicly. Some customers leave, and none of them call you a liar.

title: The Part That Comes Off
text: A component detaches under force a child can generate. Your own test found it. Nobody outside knows yet.

outcome.narration: You pull every unit and pay for the postage both ways. It is the worst quarter and the easiest decision.

choices.label: Fix it on the next production run

outcome.narration: New tooling for the next run. The units already in bedrooms stay as they are.
A sticker, on a box, about a part that comes off. You know exactly what you have done.

title: The Licence
text: A franchise everyone's children can name offers you a licence. The minimum guarantee is due whether or not it sells.

outcome.narration: The name does the selling. You pay for the name whether or not it does.

choices.label: Negotiate a lower guarantee, smaller share

outcome.narration: Less upside, and a downside you could survive. They respect that you asked.
Slower, harder, and at the end of it the character belongs to you.

title: The Vets Have Questions
text: A veterinary association publishes a note about one of your ingredients. Clinics start telling owners to switch.

outcome.narration: Nine months and real data. Clinics stop warning owners off and start stocking you.
You take it out. Some animals do not like the new version, and their owners tell you so.
You outspend the note. It stays up, and so does your revenue, for now.

title: Forty Million Views Of One Dog
text: A video of a dog losing its mind over your product goes enormous. You have six weeks of stock.

choices.label: Borrow and produce everything you can

outcome.narration: You bet the balance sheet on a dog. It is the correct bet and it is still a bet.
You run out in nine days and let the waitlist build. Nobody who signs up forgets you.

choices.label: Raise the price while demand is there

outcome.narration: The margin is superb for one quarter. The comments section has a very long memory.
